• The detection of data races requires the keeping of a history of memory accesses.

(1) the problem of data race detection is decidable; (2) there is a polynomial-time algorithm for detecting data races in programs where all memory accesses are atomic and all shared memory is initialized; (3) there are polynomial-time algorithms for detecting data races that are not detected by the first algorithm, where the amount of access information kept is bounded; (4) these algorithms can be implemented in a tool that detects at least one race when the amount of access memory is limited
the detection of data race is NP-complete in the worst case, but can be done in O(n) time in the best case, where n is the number of memory accesses in the program.
